**EatPoint 0.3.2**, a fork of [OpenNutriTracker](https://github.com/simonoppowa/OpenNutriTracker) that counts food in points: 1 point is 100 kcal of carbohydrate, protein or fat.

> **Preview build.** Installs as its own app (`io.github.grohle.eatpoint`), not on Google Play or the App Store yet. It updates 0.3.1 and earlier EatPoint builds in place, keeping your data.

## What's new in 0.3.2

**Automatic updates**
- EatPoint looks for a new version when it opens and offers to download the APK for your phone. Turn it off, or check by hand, in **Settings → Updates**. It only asks GitHub for the list of releases; nothing about you is sent.
- From this version on you won't need to come back to this page to update.

**Joining a shared household**
- "Join with a QR code" did nothing when the name field was empty, without saying why. It now asks for your name.
- The join screen starts the camera reliably, asks for permission, and says what to do if the camera can't be used.
- **Send the invite** by WhatsApp, email or any app, or copy it, when you aren't next to each other. The other person taps **Paste invite**; the whole message can be pasted as it arrived.

**Google Drive**
- When Google sign-in fails, EatPoint now shows Google's actual reason and what to check in Google Cloud, instead of "wrong password or token".

**AI assistant**
- **Use Google Gemini (free)**: one tap fills in Google's address and model, with a link to create a free key in Google AI Studio. On Gemini's free tier Google may use what you send to improve its products, as the assistant explains before you save.

## Downloads
- `EatPoint-0.3.2-arm64-v8a.apk`: for almost every phone from the last few years.
- `EatPoint-0.3.2-armeabi-v7a.apk`: for older 32-bit phones (Android 8.0+).
